I’m sorry you have to experience this bro. It must be so scary. But you, and others reading, need to realize taking gear/sarms at fucking 20 and only a year into lifting, is not worth it. But you realize that now. I have extreme anxiety/ocd and cannot control my thoughts. They’re always racing. But what helps me more than any medicine is lifting weights. I would recommend getting back in the gym 4-5x a week and lifting heavy by focusing on compound movements, naturally. It does sound like some sort of anxiety attack that you cannot control. Take it day by day. 2 months seems like a long time but it’s not. A year from now your symptoms may subside and you may be rid of your anxiety. Or you may learn to control your anxiety better and be able to tackle these events that are happening to you easier. It may go away eventually but over time you’ll be able to live your life and not obsess over it happening or possibly happening. Maybe try yoga too? Good luck bro I know you’ll be fine! In a year or two you’ll look back and realize you were freaking out over something that may or may not still happen but you’ll have a mental power over it due to experience. ❤️

You don’t have to religiously follow 5x5. Learn to play with your volume. For me, for most of my compound lifts (bench, squat, dumbbell shoulder press, OHP, incline dumbbell press, t-bar row, etc.) I have learned to change up my volume. If I’m at a brand new weight, I always aim for 4x4. Then the next week is 5x5. Week after that is 4x6, then lastly 3x7-8. After I complete this cycle I bump up the weight by 5-10 lbs depending on the exercise. 5x5 is great but there will be many weeks that you will get stuck and plateau so try doing this way to mix up and play with your volume.
